diagram_math_checks.result: With the charts constructed in proof step 3.1, choose r>0 sufficiently small that the closed disc D_r is in the source normal-form image and closed D_(r^e) is in the target image. U=phi^-1(D_r) and W=psi^-1(D_(r^e)) are open neighborhoods of x and f(x). The vertical arrows are the restricted biholomorphic charts U -> D_r and W -> D_(r^e).

Top arrow is f restricted to U, directed U -> W; bottom is P_e:D_r -> D_(r^e), z -> z^e. Step 3.1 proves psi(f(p))=phi(p)^e on U, so both downward-right composites agree. Every e-th root of a point in D_(r^e) lies in D_r, giving f(U)=W. No assertion is made about preimages outside U.

For w=rho exp(i alpha) nonzero, roots rho^(1/e) exp(i(alpha+2 pi k)/e), 0<=k<e, are distinct, have modulus less than r, and all map to w. In the cubic sketch the three dots have normalized radius 0.8 at angles 0,120,240 degrees (vertical coordinates rounded to five decimals), and w has normalized radius 0.512=0.8^3 at angle 0. Complex orientation is the usual counterclockwise one; cubing triples angles. Dashed circles indicate boundaries of open discs, and their physical sizes are explicitly schematic.

The only root of z^e=0 is 0, with order e, as in F3 and proof step 4.1. The local exponent is the ramification index e, and ramification order is e-1, checked against the existing Remarks-linked def-ramification-index-and-branch-value. For e>1 the center is a ramification point and its image is a branch value; for e=1 the theorem supplies the local biholomorphism. The addition explicitly concerns f|_U and makes no global covering claim.
Statement, Facts, all five proof steps, and original Remarks are byte-identical to the archived carrier. The figure occurs only in final Remarks and is never used to establish the theorem.
